auth.title: OAuth 2.0 | HighLevel API
highlights:
# OAuth 2.0

OAuth 2.0 is a standard protocol that authorizes a client application (like a third-party app) to access specific resources on behalf of a user, without sharing the user’s password. It’s widely used for APIs that need secure, delegated access.

HighLevel supports the Authorization Code Grant flow with v2 APIs. Below is the step-by-step procedure to understand and use the OAuth 2.0 flow.

## 1. Register an OAuth App ​

1. Go to the Marketplace and sign up for a developer account.
2. Go to My Apps, click Create App.
3. Fill in the following details: 

- APP Name: Suitable name for the app.
- APP Type: Private or Public. 

- Private Apps: For personal/internal use, not listed in the Marketplace.
- Public Apps: Visible and installable by all users once approved.

Note: We recommend starting with your app set to Private. This allows you to develop and thoroughly test its functionality in a controlled environment. Once you're confident the app is stable and complete, you can switch it to Public for broader installation and use by other accounts.
- Target User: This allows you to define who your app is intended for — in other words, who will actually be using it. For the vast majority of apps (approximately 95%), the ideal choice is `"Sub-account"` (recommended).
- Who can install: Who should be able to view and install the app from the Marketplace UI? The recommended setting is `“Both Agency & Sub-account”` to ensure maximum visibility and adoption of your app. However, if you’re building a fully white-labeled SaaS feature intended to be exclusively discovered and installed by agencies for use within their sub-accounts, you may choose to limit visibility to Agencies only.
- Listing Type: White-label recommended for marketing agencies.

4. After creating the APP you will be taken to the Profile section where you will need to add the details related to your APP. For eg; APP Logo, category, Company Name, APP Description, preview images etc.
5. After completing the profile details, please click on the Advanced Settings drop down available in the left pane and go to the auth section.
6. The Auth page will appear as shown in the screenshot below. This is where you’ll configure essential settings for your app’s OAuth integration, including scopes, redirect URLs, and client credentials.

- Scopes: Scopes define the level of access your app will have — what data it can read or what actions it can perform on behalf of the user. Each endpoint's API reference page lists the scopes it requires.

- It’s best practice to request the minimum number of scopes necessary for your app to function.
- Click on the "Select Scope" dropdown and choose the relevant scopes based on your app’s functionality.
- Redirect URL: A Redirect URL (also known as a Callback URL) is the destination where the authorization server will send the authorization code after the user installs the app.

- Enter your redirect URL in the Redirect URL field.
- Click the "Add" button to save it.
- Client Keys (ID & Secret): In the Client Keys section:

- Click the "Add" button.
- Provide a name for your client key pair.
- Upon saving, your Client ID and Client Secret will be generated.

These credentials are used to identify and authenticate your application with the OAuth server during token exchange.

Important: Be sure to copy and securely store your Client Secret immediately. After clicking "OK", you will not be able to view or copy the secret again from the UI.

## 2. Add the App to Your Desired Location ​

- Have the location/agency admin visit your Installation URL.
- Select the location to connect.
- Redirected to your Redirect URL with an Authorization Code.
- Exchange the code for an Access Token via the OAuth 2.0 Get Access Token API.
- Use the Access Token to call APIs.

## 3. Get the Installation URL ​

Inside your APP Auth Pane available inside the Advanced Settings Section you will be able to see the Install Link at the top of the Page.

Click on the Show button and you will be able to see the Installation URLs which you will be using to install the APP.

Depending on your usecase and account setup you can either use the standard or the whitelabel version of the Installation URL.

Refer to the below steps to install the APP:

1. Copy the Installation URL and open it in your browser.
2. In case you are not logged in to your GHL account it will ask you to login to your account.

- In case you are logged in it will show a page showcasing the accounts.

3. Select the account you want to install the APP in.
4. When a user grants access, their browser is redirected to the specified redirect URI, and the Authorization Code is passed inside the `code` query parameter. If you included a `state` value in the Installation URL, it is returned unchanged in the `state` query parameter.

https://myapp.com/oauth/callback/highlevel?code=7676cjcbdc6t76cdcbkjcd09821jknnkj&state=RANDOM_SINGLE_USE_VALUE 

This URL demonstrates a typical OAuth callback scenario for a HighLevel integration. The `code` parameter included in the query string is essential for completing the authorization flow.

### Using the `state` Parameter ​

We recommend using `state` to protect your callback against cross-site request forgery (CSRF). Both `/oauth/chooselocation` and `/v2/oauth/chooselocation` support it.

1. Before sending the user to the Installation URL, generate a cryptographically random, short-lived, single-use value and bind it to the user's session.
2. Append it to the Installation URL as the URL-encoded `state` query parameter. Use printable ASCII characters only, for example a hex or base64url-encoded value.
3. On your callback, reject the request if `state` is missing or does not exactly match the stored value, and invalidate the stored value before exchanging the code.

### Authorization Code Rules ​

- The redirect URI must exactly match a redirect URI registered for your app.
- Exchange the code using your app's `client_id` and `client_secret`.
- Authorization codes expire after five minutes and can be used only once.

PKCE/S256 is not currently supported for the Marketplace app installation authorization flow. PKCE support for External Authentication applies to a separate flow and does not replace the `state` validation described above.

...

## 5. Exchange Authorization Code for Access Token ​

Once you have received the Authorization code on your redirect URl you are expected to use Get Access Token API endpoint to generate the Acces Token which you can then use to run the API endpoints.

Sample Payload:

curl -X POST "https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/oauth/token" \ 

 -H "Accept: application/json" \ 

 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 

 -d '{ 

 "client_id": "665c6bb13d4e5364bdec0e2f-mawqjyjd", 

 "client_secret": "74032272-7f45-4e07-8717-5e1ddbfe3de0", 

 "grant_type": "authorization_code", 

 "code": "363fe3f086e2db02bb9c34722902d21f76c9b217", 

 "user_type": "Company", 

 "redirect_uri": "https://myapp.com/oauth/callback/highlevel" 

 "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJhdXRoQ2xhc3MiOiJDb20", 

 "token_type": "Bearer", 

 "expires_in": 86399, 

 "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJhdXRoQ2xhc3MiOiJDb21w", 

 "scope": "calendars.readonly calendars/events.readonly calendars.write calendars/events.write calendars/groups.readonly calendars/groups.write calendars/resources.readonly calendars/resources.write", 

 "refreshTokenId": "685a9cc9f7434ae2fc66c31d", 

 "userType": "Company", 

 "companyId": "GNb7aIv4rQFVb9iwNl5K", 

 "isBulkInstallation": true, 

 "userId": "Rg6BRRiHh7dS9gJy3W8a" 

## 6. Refresh Token Usage ​

As shown in the previous response, the Access Token expires after 86,399 seconds, which is approximately 24 hours. This means you'll need to regenerate a new Access Token once it expires to continue making API requests.

However, regenerating an Access Token using the authorization code requires repeating the entire installation process, which can be time-consuming. To simplify this, we also provide a Refresh Token along with the Access Token.

The Refresh Token is valid for up to one year, or until it is used. Once you use a Refresh Token to obtain a new Access Token, the original Refresh Token becomes invalid, and the response will include a new Refresh Token along with the new Access Token. If left unused, the Refresh Token will remain valid for one year.

To generate a new Access Token using your existing Refresh Token, use the following API endpoint: Get Access Token

- Access Tokens expire after ~24 hours.
- Refresh Tokens are valid for 1 year or until used.
- Use Refresh Token to obtain a new Access Token without reinstallation.

...

## 7. Types of Access Token ​

In HighLevel we have 2 types of Access Token depending on the type of APP you have installed and who has installed the APP.

1. Access Token with User Type as Agency: This Type of Access Token will be utilized to run the APIs related to the Agency Functionalities. For eg; Create Sub-Account API.

Sample Response:

...

2. Access Token with User Type as Location: This Type of Access Token will be utilized to run the APIs related to the Sub-Account or Location Functionalities. For eg; Create Contact API.

 "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJqdGkiOiI2ODViZDRiNW", 

 "token_type": "Bearer",

## HighLevel API Documentation

 The official API documentation provides information about available endpoints, authentication, request parameters, response formats, and supported API versions. Developers can use this documentation to:  

- Explore available API endpoints.  
- Review authentication requirements.  
- Check supported API versions.  
- Build and maintain custom integrations.  
- Understand endpoint-specific restrictions.

Note: New legacy API key generation is being phased out. Private Integration Tokens and OAuth 2.0 are the recommended authentication methods.

## How to Use Versioned API Documentation

Versioned API documentation allows developers to reference the correct API version when building or maintaining integrations.  

1. Open the HighLevel API Documentation.  
2. Select the required API version using the version switcher.    
3. Review the available endpoints, parameters, and response formats.  
4. Use the appropriate version when developing or updating integrations.

API V3 is available for supported endpoints. Availability varies by endpoint.

...

## API Access Across HighLevel Plans

HighLevel offers API access across its subscription plans, including Starter, Unlimited, and Founder.

Both OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens (PIT) are available across plans. However, access to specific API endpoints depends on subscription eligibility, permissions, and scopes.

 API Availability by Plan 

| API Capability | Starter ($97/month) | Unlimited ($297/month) | Founder ($497/month) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OAuth 2.0 | Available | Available | Available |
| Private Integration Tokens | Available | Available | Available |
| Standard API Endpoints | Available* | Available | Available |
| Higher-Tier Restricted Endpoints | Restricted | Restricted | Subject to endpoint eligibility |

*Standard endpoint access is subject to applicable permissions and endpoint-specific restrictions.

For current subscription details, visit HighLevel Pricing.

...

## API Authentication Methods

HighLevel supports two primary authentication methods for modern API integrations.

Private Integration Tokens (PIT)

Private Integration Tokens allow developers to securely connect internal applications to HighLevel. They are suitable for account-specific integrations and allow permissions to be managed through assigned scopes.

OAuth 2.0

OAuth 2.0 allows applications to request authorized access to HighLevel accounts. It is commonly used for public integrations, Marketplace applications, and applications requiring user authorization.

Note: The availability of an authentication method does not guarantee access to every API endpoint.

For setup instructions, see Private Integrations: Everything You Need to Know.

auth.title: Introduction | HighLevel API
highlights:
## Authentication ​

All requests are authenticated using OAuth 2.0. You'll exchange your credentials for an access token, then include that token in the `Authorization` header of each request:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN 

Access tokens are scoped, so an application only receives the permissions it has been granted.

auth.title: Private Integrations | HighLevel API
highlights:
## Key Advantages of Private Integrations ​

- Simple: Generate Private Integration tokens from your account settings and manage them with ease.
- Secure: You get to restrict the scopes/permissions that a developer can access on your account.

Private Integrations are available for both Agencies and Sub-Accounts.

## What's the difference between Private Integrations and API Keys? ​

| Private Integrations | API Keys |
| --- | --- |
| More Secure: You get to restrict the scopes/permissions that a developer can access on your account | Less Secure: A developer gets unrestricted access to all your account data |
| State-of-art: Private Integrations allows you to access API v2.0 which is state of the art | Out-dated: API Keys work on API v1.0 which has reached end-of-life and is no longer maintained |
| More Features: API v2.0 has more powerful APIs | Less Features: API v1.0 has limited APIs |

## What's the difference between Private Integrations and OAuth2 Access Tokens? ​

Private Integrations, to put it simply, are static/fixed OAuth2 Access Tokens.

| Private Integrations | Access Tokens |
| --- | --- |
| Generated from the UI: Private Integration token can be generated easily from the UI | Programmatic Generation: API Tokens are generated by exchanging OAuth access code for the tokens using Get Access Token API |
| Static/Fixed: Private Integration Tokens are static/fixed and do not automatically refresh unless you rotate them from the UI | Refreshed Daily: Access Tokens expire daily and need to be refreshed |

## How do I use Private Integrations? ​

Private Integration tokens are used in the Authorization header, just like other Access Tokens.

Example:

curl --request GET \ 

 --url https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/locations/ve9EPM428h8vShlRW1KT \ 

 --header 'Accept: application/json' \ 

 --header 'Authorization: Bearer <YOUR PRIVATE INTEGRATION TOKEN>' \ 

 --header 'Version: 2021-07-28'

...

## How do I create a new Private Integration? ​

Step 1: Click on "Create new Integration"  Step 2: Give your Private Integration a name and description to help you and your team identify what it's for.  Step 3: Select the scopes/permissions that you want the private integration to have access to on your agency account. Ensure that you are selecting only the required scopes for better data security.  Step 4: Copy the token generated and share it with your third-party app developer.

> Note: Please ensure that you are sharing the token with trusted parties only. Do not share it publicly.  Don't forget to copy the token generated as you won't be able to do it again later.

> HighLevel API is the REST API of the HighLevel platform (ad-publishing, affiliate-manager, agent-studio, associations, blogs, brand-boards, businesses, calendars, campaigns, chat-widget, clientportal-ai, companies, ...). This is an LLM-friendly index of its reference documentation, generated from the OpenAPI specs at build time.

- Base URL: https://services.leadconnectorhq.com (append the endpoint path).
- Every request must send a `Version` header whose value is the API version name, e.g. `Version: v3`. Published versions: v3 (latest), 2023-02-21, 2021-07-28, 2021-04-15.
- Every authenticated request sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

## Authentication

- OAuth 2.0 access token: issued to an app through the authorization-code flow (POST /oauth/token exchanges the code or a refresh token). A token is issued either for a Sub-Account (location) or for an Agency (company).
- Private Integration Token (PIT): a static token created in the Sub-Account or Agency settings with a chosen set of scopes; it is sent exactly like an access token. Endpoints marked "OAuth access token only" reject PITs.
- Sub-Account vs Agency: every endpoint states which token type it accepts. An Agency access token can be exchanged for a Sub-Account token with POST /oauth/location-token.
- Scopes: every endpoint lists the scopes it requires; the token must carry all of them (requested during OAuth authorization, or selected when the PIT is created).

## Instructions for LLMs

- Default to the latest version, v3, unless the user names another version.
- Always send `Version: <version>` with the version whose documentation you used (`Version: v3` for the latest). Never mix endpoints or schemas from different versions in one integration.
- Call https://services.leadconnectorhq.com followed by the endpoint path; replace `{param}` placeholders with path parameter values.
- Pick the token type, OAuth/PIT method and scopes from the endpoint's Auth line.
- Find endpoints in the version's llms.txt, then read the service `.md` file or the endpoint `.md` file for the full request and response schema.

gate.title: Private Integration Tokens (PITs) Now Available for Sandbox & Trial Accounts | HighLevel Changelog
highlights:
# Private Integration Tokens (PITs) Now Available for Sandbox & Trial Accounts

We’ve enabled Private Integration Tokens (PITs) for Sandbox and Trial accounts, allowing developers and agencies to test their custom integrations end-to-end against HighLevel APIs before going live.

✅ What This Means

Sandbox and Trial accounts can now:

- Create and use Private Integration Tokens
- Authenticate custom integrations safely
- Test API workflows without using production accounts
- Avoid manual support intervention

This removes the previous restriction that blocked PIT creation for these account types.

🔒 Built for Safe Testing

To ensure platform stability and prevent abuse, PIT usage in Sandbox and Trial accounts operates under conservative, leadership-approved API rate limits:

- Burst Limit

: 

25 requests per 10 seconds
- Daily Limit: 10,000 requests

These limits apply across all Private Integration Tokens in the account (limits do not multiply per token).

⚡ Automatic Upgrade Handling

When a Trial account upgrades to a paid plan:

- API limits are automatically updated to standard production limits
- No manual intervention is required
- Entitlements update immediately

💬 Need Higher Limits for Testing?

If you’re building a serious integration and need higher daily quotas for testing, contact Support to request a temporary increase (marketplace@gohighlevel.com).

The HighLevel Partner Network connects qualified HighLevel founders with businesses looking for expertise, services, and support. This article explains how to join the Partner Network, how matching works, and how Partner status and customer connections contribute to future opportunities.

# What is the HighLevel Partner Network?

The HighLevel Partner Network is a program that connects businesses with qualified HighLevel partners who can help them use the platform effectively. Businesses are matched with Partners based on their specific needs and the expertise of available Partners.

For qualified Partners, the network provides opportunities to connect with potential customers, establish service relationships, and grow their businesses.

## Partner Eligibility and Qualification

Joining the Partner Network requires an eligible Founder Plan subscription and successful completion of the qualification process. Meeting these requirements allows founders to become qualified Partners.

Visit: https://partners.gohighlevel.com/

## How Partner Matching Works

Partner matching connects businesses with qualified Partners whose expertise aligns with their needs. Recommendations are personalized to help businesses identify suitable service providers.

Beginning January 1, 2027, HighLevel will start matching businesses with qualified Partners.

- Each business receives five personalized Partner recommendations.  
- Recommendations are based on business needs and available Partner expertise.  
- Partner status influences weighting within the matching algorithm.

Being recommended creates an opportunity to connect with a potential customer but does not guarantee a new client.

## Partner Status Levels

Partner status recognizes growth in HighLevel wallet spend across connected customer accounts. Performance is evaluated relative to other Partners in the network, and higher status levels increase matching weight.

## Frequently Asked Questions

#### Q: Does subscribing to the Founder Plan automatically enroll me in the Partner Network?

No. The Founder Plan is HighLevel's $497/month subscription, while the Partner Network is a separate, optional program. You must opt in and complete the applicable qualification requirements to become a Partner.

#### Q: Is there an additional membership fee to join the Partner Network?

No. Eligible Founder Plan customers can apply to join the Partner Network without paying a separate Partner Network membership fee.

#### Q: How do I opt into the HighLevel Partner Network?

You can submit the opt-in form through the Partner tab in your account or visit  https://partners.gohighlevel.com/ 

 An active Founder Plan subscription is required.

#### Q: What happens after I submit the opt-in form?

Once your active Founder Plan has been confirmed, you will be assigned a Partner Growth Specialist and receive a welcome email outlining the next steps, including the applicable assessments and onboarding call.

#### Q: What are the requirements to become a qualified HighLevel Partner?

You must have an active Founder Plan subscription, pass the Builder Exam, Advisor Exam, and AI Implementation Exam (unless an exemption applies), and complete onboarding with a Partner Growth Specialist.

#### Q: Can existing HighLevel customers qualify for assessment exemptions?

Yes. Certain existing customers may qualify for exemptions based on their account history, business model, and applicable qualification requirements.

#### Q: Can individual service providers join the Partner Network?

Yes. Individual Experts can join the Partner Network. They must personally complete the required assessments unless an approved exemption applies.

#### Q: Can Solutions Provider team members split the required assessments, or does one person need to complete all three?

Solutions Providers can divide the three required assessments among team members based on their roles and expertise. One person does not need to complete all three assessments.

As long as all three assessments are successfully completed by team members linked to the same organization, and the organization completes its onboarding requirements, the Solutions Provider can meet the qualification requirements.

#### Q: What is the purpose of the Partner Growth Specialist onboarding call?

The call helps evaluate your readiness to serve customers and provides an opportunity to discuss your business, services, ideal customers, and areas of expertise. This information helps establish your Partner profile for matching.

#### Q: When will Partner matching begin?

Partner matching is currently scheduled to begin on January 1, 2027.

...

#### Q: Does becoming a qualified Partner guarantee leads or customers?

No. Qualification makes you eligible for matching opportunities, but HighLevel does not guarantee a specific number of matches, customers, projects, or revenue.

...

#### Q: Does the free Certified Admin certification provide Partner matching opportunities?

No. The free Certified Admin certification demonstrates HighLevel proficiency but does not include Partner Network matching opportunities. Matching requires separate Partner Network qualification.

#### Q: Do businesses have to pay to receive Partner recommendations?

No. Partner matching is free for businesses. However, Partners may independently charge for their services, and any service-related fees are handled directly between the business and the Partner.

#### Q: Who determines the pricing for services provided by a Partner?

Partners set their own service pricing. The Partner and customer agree directly on pricing, project scope, deliverables, and payment arrangements.

## Sell on Marketplace : Auto-created Developer Accounts (Agency Admins)

When an agency admin selects Sell on Marketplace, the system checks whether the admin already has a developer account.

If the admin does not have a developer account, HighLevel:

1. Creates a developer profile in the background using existing account details.

2. Redirects the admin to sign in.

3. Prompts the admin to:

 - Enter their password

 - Accept the developer terms and conditions

 - Verify a one-time password (OTP) sent by email

4. Signs the admin into the new developer account and continues the Marketplace listing flow.

  You do not need to complete a manual developer signup form.

mcp.title: Guide on How to Setup and Use the HighLevel MCP Server : HighLevel Support Portal
highlights:
Modified on: Sun, 15 Nov, 2026 at 2:10 AM

Connect your AI assistant to HighLevel so it can find CRM records and perform supported actions from your instructions. The HighLevel MCP Server, also called the LeadConnector MCP Server, connects through OAuth: sign in, choose the sub-account or sub-accounts to include, and approve the requested permissions.

This guide covers setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, Muse, and Grok Bot, along with how to work across authorized sub-accounts and discover available operations.

...

# What is the HighLevel MCP Server?

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It gives AI assistants a standard way to discover and use tools from connected applications. With the HighLevel MCP Server, your assistant can work with supported CRM data and actions without you needing to know the underlying API.

The active catalog includes more than 600 read, create, update, and delete operations across 38 domains. The operations available to your connection depend on the OAuth scopes and permissions you approve.

## Before You Connect

You need access to the HighLevel sub-account or sub-accounts you want to connect and a supported AI client. ChatGPT users can find the official HighLevel plugin in Plugins. Muse and Grok Bot also offer officially listed apps. For custom MCP connections, use the corresponding URL below.

| AI client | Connection method |
| --- | --- |
| Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2` |
| ChatGPT, Codex, and other compatible OpenAI clients | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/` |
| Cursor | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/cursor/v2` |
| Muse | Connect the official app in Muse; its OAuth endpoint is `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/muse/v2/` |
| Grok Bot | Add HighLevel from Connect apps |
| ChatGPT | Open ChatGPT → Plugins, search for HighLevel, and connect through OAuth. No manual MCP server URL is required. |

These connections use OAuth. During authorization, sign in to LeadConnector, select the available sub-account(s), and approve the requested scopes. All connection options use the current active LeadConnector MCP operation catalog.

...

## Working with One or Multiple Sub-accounts

### Single sub-account

A single-sub-account connection is bound to the sub-account you choose during OAuth authorization for the lifetime of that connection.

### Agency connection

Where agency-wide access is available, you can connect once and work across the sub-accounts selected during installation.

1. Choose the sub-accounts during installation. Select one, several, or all of the sub-accounts offered by the agency installation.  
2. Name the sub-account in your request. If the intended sub-account is unclear, the assistant uses `list_locations` and asks you to choose.  
3. Switch within the same chat. Ask about another authorized sub-account without reconnecting.

For example:

List the contacts tagged “vip-2026” in Downtown Clinic, then compare the count with Uptown Med Spa.

The assistant resolves the sub-account names, queries each sub-account separately, and compares the results. Every request targets one sub-account and is authorized against your installation. The connection cannot access sub-accounts you did not include.

Availability: Single-sub-account connections are available today. Agency-wide connections are rolling out through the multi-sub-account, or bulk, installation option. If installation offers only one sub-account, the multi-sub-account option is not enabled for your app yet.

Watch the multiple-sub-account walkthrough.

## How the Four MCP Tools Work

The server exposes four unified tools. Your assistant uses these tools to find and run the operations available to your connection.

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `list_locations` | Find the sub-accounts available to the connection, or return its single bound sub-account. |
| `search_operations` | Discover active operations for the task, including record searches and read, create, update, and delete actions. |
| `describe_operation` | Check an operation's inputs, example payload, required scopes, and safety information. |
| `execute_operation` | Run an operation within OAuth scopes, permissions, sub-account boundaries, and built-in safety checks. |

You can ask your assistant to use `search_operations` to check what is available to your connection at any time.

## What You Can Do

The active catalog covers the following areas. Availability depends on your OAuth scopes and permissions.

| Area | Examples of supported operations |
| --- | --- |
| Contacts | Search and manage contacts, duplicate lookup, tags, notes, tasks, followers, campaigns, appointments, business assignment, and workflow enrollment. |
| Conversations & Messages | Manage conversations; read and send messages; work with attachments, scheduled messages, status updates, recordings, transcriptions, exports, and typing indicators. |
| Opportunities & Pipelines | Work with pipelines, lost reasons, opportunity searches, create/update/delete/upsert actions, followers, and status changes. |
| Calendars & Appointments | Work with calendars, groups, appointments, events, notes, notifications, free and blocked slots, resources, availability schedules, services, service locations, and bookings. |
| Payments | Manage coupons, payment provider configuration, integrations, orders, fulfillment, recorded payments, subscriptions, and transactions. |
| Products & Store | Work with products, prices, collections, inventory, reviews, store placement, shipping carriers, zones and rates, and store settings. |
| Invoices, Estimates & Documents | Work with invoices, estimates, templates, schedules, manual payments, send and void actions, invoice creation from estimates, proposals, and document links. |
| Social Planner | Work with social accounts, posts, comments, categories, tags, CSV imports, category queues, calendar views, edit sessions, and statistics. |

...

|

...

| Workflows | List and search workflows; browse step types; read, create, validate, update, publish, and delete workflow definitions; and read execution logs and step ... Contact enrollment and removal use contact operations.

...

It reports the results back in natural language.

## Permissions and Security

- You select the sub-accounts. Each request is authorized against the installation and can access only a sub-account included in that connection.  
- OAuth scopes limit actions. The assistant can perform only the operations allowed by your grant.  
- Sensitive actions have additional checks. Sensitive and irreversible operations are subject to confirmation and safety checks before execution.  
- You control ongoing access. Review or revoke the connection's access from your LeadConnector account.

...

#### Q: Do I need a Private Integration Token?

The client connections in this guide use OAuth. Complete the LeadConnector sign-in and consent flow to authorize access; you do not need to manually create or rotate a token for these connections.

...

Ask your assistant to search for the operation you need.

#### Q: Can my assistant create, update, or delete records?

Yes, where the operation is supported and your OAuth grant permits it. Sensitive and irreversible actions also have confirmation and safety checks.

mcp.title: mcp | HighLevel API
highlights:
# HighLevel MCP Server

Stop clicking. Start asking.

Your next booking, follow-up, or invoice can start with a sentence. Connect HighLevel to your AI assistant, then ask it to find a contact, book an appointment, send a message, update a deal, or schedule a social post. The assistant works directly with your HighLevel account, so you can get work done from the conversation you’re already having.

More than 700 actions across 38 HighLevel features give you room to hand off everyday work:

- Follow up while the context is fresh. Look up a lead’s messages, check their appointments, and send your reply from the same chat.
- Turn a decision into action. Create and send an invoice, update a deal, or add a follow-up task without opening each record yourself.
- Keep marketing moving. Schedule social posts, review email campaign results, and manage promotions.
- Skip screen navigation. The assistant searches and updates records directly, without opening HighLevel pages or reading screenshots. See why use MCP.
- Keep access on your terms. Connect the sub-accounts you want to use and approve the permissions. Agencies with multi-sub-account installation enabled can switch between connected sub-accounts in one chat.

No API key to create or paste. Sign in with your HighLevel login, connect your sub-account, and try your first request.

...

## Why use MCP instead of asking AI to click through HighLevel? ​

Give your assistant a direct connection to the work. With MCP, it can ask HighLevel for records and act on the results without navigating menus, opening each contact, or scrolling through screens.

For a request like “Find Jane, book her consultation, and text her the details,” the assistant can look up her contact, check calendar availability, create the appointment, and send the message through HighLevel’s supported operations. That removes the page navigation between those steps.

| What matters to you | AI using the HighLevel interface | HighLevel MCP Server |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Getting the work done | Navigates pages and interacts with on-screen controls | Calls supported HighLevel actions directly, with no app pages to load |
| Finding the right records | Uses the search and lists exposed in the interface | Uses record searches and filters where supported; can fetch further pages of results |
| Working with details | Reads values from the interface | Receives record details directly and uses those records in the next action |
| When the layout changes | May need to adjust to moved buttons, menus, or dialogs | Calls API operations independently of the app’s visual layout |
| Controlling access | Works through the browser session’s access | Uses the connection’s approved permissions and checks the selected sub-account for each execution |
| Reviewing a change | Depends on the assistant and the screen’s controls | Supports a preview of the proposed request before the action is sent |

Use MCP for the everyday work in the capability table: looking up information, updating records, booking, messaging, and managing your business from chat. Browser use remains useful for visual work or features the connection doesn’t expose.

Previews show the proposed request; they don’t guarantee the action will succeed. Approval prompts and how results appear depend on your assistant.

## Get connected in three steps ​

1. Add HighLevel to your assistant using the app or address below.
2. Sign in with your HighLevel login, and choose the sub-account (or sub-accounts) to connect.
3. Approve, then ask: “Show me the last 5 contacts I added.”

| Your assistant | What to add | Step-by-step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ChatGPT | The official HighLevel app in ChatGPT | Connect ChatGPT |
| Claude (Claude.ai, Claude Cowork) | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2` | Connect Claude |
| Muse | The official HighLevel app in Muse | Connect Muse |
| Grok Bot | The official HighLevel app in Grok Bot | Connect Grok Bot |
| Claude Code, Codex, Cursor | The developer setup for your tool | Claude Code · Codex · Cursor |

Copy addresses exactly as shown. The sign-in page is on `leadconnectorhq.com`, a HighLevel domain, so use your usual HighLevel login there.

...

The table covers 717 supported actions across 38 feature areas, grouped by the HighLevel menu. Available actions depend on your connection’s permissions and the features enabled in your sub-account. An action is one operation, such as finding a contact or creating an appointment; a request can combine several.

...

## Stay in control ​

The assistant only gets the access you give it, and HighLevel checks that access every time it acts.

- You choose the sub-accounts. The assistant can only work in the sub-accounts you selected when you connected.
- You choose the permissions. It can only take actions your approved permissions allow, and each action is checked again when it runs.
- No passwords or API keys to share. You sign in on HighLevel’s own sign-in page. Your assistant never sees your password.
- Preview before anything changes. Ask the assistant to preview a change first. The server can return the proposed request without running that action. A preview does not simulate the result or confirm that HighLevel will accept the change.
- Approve each change. Assistants that support approvals can ask you before every action that changes your data. Keep that setting on.
- Workflows start as drafts. New workflows are saved as drafts, so nothing goes live until you publish. Review them in the workflow builder first.
- Disconnect at any time. Remove the connection in your assistant, or revoke the app from your HighLevel account.

Actions affect your real account: sending a message initiates delivery, deleting a record can remove it permanently, publishing a workflow activates its triggers, and purchasing a phone number can incur charges. Try unfamiliar requests in a test sub-account first.

...

## How it works ​

HighLevel gives your assistant four tools to find and use the actions available to your connection. It can discover an action, read its requirements, and execute it without loading hundreds of separate action definitions upfront.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_locations` | Lists the sub-accounts this connection can use, so the right one is chosen |
| `search_operations` | Finds the right action for a request. It only returns actions your permissions allow |
| `describe_operation` | Shows what an action needs, with an example, the permissions it requires, and its safety information |
| `execute_operation` | Runs the action after checking permissions and sub-account access, or previews it without sending anything |

New supported actions can be discovered through the same tools. If an action needs a permission you haven’t approved, reconnect to grant it. Availability also depends on your sub-account’s enabled features.

...

...

### What is MCP? ​

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for connecting AI assistants to the apps you use. HighLevel uses it to connect compatible assistants that support remote Streamable HTTP servers and HighLevel’s sign-in flow.

### Can the assistant do everything I can do in HighLevel? ​

It supports more than 700 actions across the features listed above. Coverage varies by feature: for example, it can read your published Agent Studio agents, while supported workflow actions include building and publishing. Ask what’s available for your connection, or tell us what’s missing.

...

### Do I need an API key or a Private Integration token? ​

No. You connect by signing in with your HighLevel login, choosing your sub-account(s), and approving the requested permissions. There’s no key to create, paste, or rotate.

...

### Is this the same as the Developer MCP Server? ​

No. This server connects AI assistants to the data in your HighLevel sub-accounts. The Marketplace Developer MCP Server is a separate tool that helps developers build and release Marketplace apps.

highlights:
## What is the HighLevel MCP for Anthropic?

The HighLevel MCP for Anthropic is an OAuth-based Model Context Protocol endpoint specifically designed for Claude clients. MCP (Model Context Protocol) enables AI assistants like Claude to connect to external data sources and tools through a standardized interface.

This endpoint provides access to the complete HighLevel operation catalog — 625 operations across 40 domains — representing a substantial expansion beyond the limited-scope surface of the original universal MCP endpoint. The Anthropic endpoint uses a dedicated OAuth application that grants the widest scope set available, while maintaining complete user control over which permissions are granted.

The endpoint follows a per-client MCP pattern, with the URL structure:

https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2

This approach allows different AI clients to maintain isolated OAuth grants, ensuring that scopes granted to Claude remain separate from scopes granted to other clients like ChatGPT or future integrations.
